claim.pdf_says: >* next statement            ...            >*   to next statement      (the words 'next statement' are printed in bold monospace inside the PERFORM code example)
claim.markdown_says: >* **next statement**            ...            >*   to **next statement**      (inside a ``` fenced code block)
claim.why_it_matters: The bold markers are emitted as literal '**' characters inside a fenced code block, where markdown emphasis is not interpreted, so the rendered code sample reads '>* **next statement**' - four characters that do not exist in the standard. The very same code example continues onto p1125, where the identical bold words ARE transcribed plainly ('>* next statement', '>*   to next statement'), so one COBOL example is transcribed two different ways across the page break.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim's quotations are exact.

PDF (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1124/spec_p1124.png, D.16.5 'Inline exception processing', printed page 1094): the monospace PERFORM example prints two lines whose trailing words are set in BOLD monospace while the rest of the sample is regular monospace - '>* next statement' (3rd line of the block, after 'COMPUTE something') and '>*   to next statement' (last line of the WHEN COMMON group). I read the glyphs directly: there is no asterisk pair on the page; the only asterisks printed are the comment indicators themselves ('>*' on most lines, and '*>' on the two FINALLY lines). The bold is pure typographic emphasis applied to the words 'next statement'.

Markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, canonical file, not just the workunit slice): the fence opens at line 45183 and closes at line 45206. Inside it, line 45186 is '       >* **next statement**' and line 45200 is '       >*   to **next statement**'. Because these lines sit inside a ``` fenced code block, CommonMark does not interpret emphasis - the four '*' characters render literally. So the transcribed COBOL sample contains characters that do not exist in the standard, and any tooling that extracts code samples from the transcription picks up '>* **next statement**'.

This is not reflow, hyphenation, page-break furniture, or a rendering nicety: the failure is precisely that the emphasis markup does NOT render, so a formatting intent becomes literal text content inside a code sample. Nothing is missing or reordered, and no normative rule depends on this informative Annex D example, so 'cosmetic' is the right severity - but it is a genuine textual discrepancy, not a formatting-only difference.

The internal-inconsistency half of the claim also checks out. On p1125 the PDF prints the same phrase in bold three times - '>* next statement' (first line), 'RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT >* go to next statement', and '>*   to next statement' - and specs/ISO_COBOL.md transcribes all three PLAINLY, with no '**' (lines 45222, 45228, 45237). Same source typography, two opposite transcription conventions, 36 lines apart in the same file.

One detail in the claim's framing is imprecise; see corrected_description.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with one framing correction. The '**' corruption is real: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 45186 ('       >* **next statement**') and 45200 ('       >*   to **next statement**') sit inside the fenced block spanning lines 45183-45206, so the asterisks render as literal text. The PDF (printed p1094) sets those words in bold monospace with no asterisks.

Correction: the p1125 block is NOT a continuation of the block containing the '**'. Page 1124 holds TWO examples - the first (the '**'-corrupted one) runs PERFORM ... END-PERFORM and closes on p1124; a second example then begins at the foot of p1124 ('You could avoid termination with something like this:' / 'PERFORM' / 'COMPUTE something >* results in a size error') and it is THAT second example whose tail continues onto p1125. So the inconsistency is between two adjacent near-identical examples, not between two halves of one example split by the page break. The substance is unaffected and arguably stronger: the same bold phrase occurs twice in example 1 (both transcribed with '**') and three times in example 2 (all three transcribed plainly, including the additional occurrence in 'RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT >* go to next statement' at line 45228, which the claim did not mention).

Recommended repair: strip the two '**' pairs at lines 45186 and 45200 so the code samples carry only the characters the standard prints, matching the convention already used everywhere else in this pair of examples.
